questions.title: Who will Morocco's king appoint as prime minister following the country's 2026 parliamentary election?
questions.background: Morocco's prime minister leads the government and is appointed by the king.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The Moroccan royal palace's public announcement, as documented in reliable news reporting. Resolution Condition : Resolve to the first person appointed prime minister and tasked with forming a government following Morocco's 2026 parliamentary election. Accepted Answer Format : The appointee's name or commonly used surname.
questions.current_reasoning: MAJOR 2026-09-24 STRUCTURAL LOCK: Official provisional parliamentary results announced Thursday Sept 24 by Interior Minister Abdelouafi Laftit (Reuters, AFP, Al Jazeera, Le360, The National, Ynet, DW, Straits Times) confirm PAM won first place outright with 97 of 395 seats (up from 87 in 2021), well ahead of RNI (66), Istiqlal (65), and PJD (54) on 38.02% turnout. Under Article 47 of Morocco's 2011 Constitution, King Mohammed VI MUST appoint the Head of Government from the winning party (PAM), zeroing out non-PAM contenders Mohamed Chaouki (RNI), Nizar Baraka (Istiqlal), and Abdelilah Benkirane (PJD). Inside PAM, Sept 24 Moroccan and international coverage (Le360, AFP/La Libre, Reuters, The National, Commonspace) uniformly frames a very tight two-horse race between: (1) Fouzi Lekjaa (0.30 -> 0.45) — Budget Minister, FRMF President, and 2030 World Cup boss who made a surprise pre-election entry into PAM's Political Bureau (qualifying him under Article 47 for what media dub the 'World Cup government') and whom El Mansouri hailed today as 'la vedette des elections'; and (2) Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri (0.26 -> 0.41) — PAM's formal National Coordinator (King Mohammed VI has appointed the winning party's formal head 3-for-3 times since 2011), Marrakech mayor, and Territorial Planning Minister who signaled readiness at today's Rabat press conference ('ce serait pour moi un grand honneur', noting the King's support for women's rights as she would become Morocco's first female PM) while keeping all coalition doors open. Adding PAM collective-leadership co-member and Youth Minister Mohamed Mehdi Bensaid (0.08, floated #3 in Sept 24 press and flanked El Mansouri today), senior PAM Employment Minister Younes Sekkouri (0.03), and Justice Minister/former PAM SG Abdellatif Ouahbi (0.01), leaving 0.02 residual for other PAM figures (e.g., Fatima Saadi, Ahmed Akhchichen).
watch_keywords: King Mohammed VI appoints prime minister
questions.COORDINATOR_CRITICAL_FACT: COORDINATOR_CRITICAL_FACT (LOCAL SEP 26 AL JAZEERA/TOI CONFIRMED!): Final Morocco election results confirmed: PAM #1 (97 seats), RNI fell from 102 to 66, PJD surged to 54 (will stay in opposition), Istiqlal #3; King Mohammed VI must appoint PM from PAM (Article 47). Al Jazeera Sep 26 explicitly names Fouzi Lekjaa and Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri as top candidates. Search Sep 26 Moroccan press (Hespress, Le360, Medias24, TelQuel, Maghreb Arab Press) for any Royal Palace audience/appointment or leak!

questions.title: Who will Aston Martin announce as Lance Stroll's teammate for the 2027 Formula One season?
questions.background: Aston Martin has not yet confirmed its complete race-driver lineup for the 2027 Formula One season.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Aston Martin's official announcement confirming its complete race-driver lineup for the 2027 Formula One season, corroborated by Formula One or reputable news reporting. Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the driver named alongside Lance Stroll in the first such announcement published by December 31, 2026. A confirmed race-seat contract is sufficient; the driver need not have competed in a 2027 race. Reserve, test, and advisory roles do not qualify. Accepted Answer Format : The driver's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Updating on 2026-09-12 from GPblog (Aug 29-30), PlanetF1 (Sept 10 Madrid FIA press conference), and Sept 12 Spanish GP qualifying (Reuters/Arab News/Straits Times): Virtually all remaining external candidates are now off the 2027 grid—in addition to Verstappen (Red Bull), Norris (McLaren), Russell (Mercedes), and Sainz/Albon (Williams), GPblog confirms Sergio Perez (0.11 -> 0.04) remains on his multi-year Cadillac deal after no rival doors opened, and Oliver Bearman (0.06 -> 0.03) is locked in as Haas's 2027 team leader. GPblog also reports Aston Martin and Fernando Alonso are 'very likely to continue,' raising Alonso 0.55 -> 0.65. However, we cap Alonso at 0.65 (strict anti-overconfidence) because he explicitly told reporters in Madrid on Sept 10 that an announcement is 'not soon' ('no urgency'), is 45, and Aston Martin's 2026 car remains mired at the back (Alonso qualified P18 and Stroll P22/no time at Madrid today). If Alonso retires or shifts to an advisory role, top fallbacks are Honda-linked free agent Yuki Tsunoda (0.10; subbing strongly for Racing Bulls with P10 at Monza and Q2 in Madrid), Haas-exiting GP winner and Stroll friend Esteban Ocon (0.07; Q2 in Madrid), Perez (0.04), Bearman (0.03), and 0.11 residual (Crawford/Drugovich/Lawson/Bottas).

questions.title: Which court, if any, will grant Christa Pike a stay on the day of her scheduled September 30, 2026 execution?
questions.background: Christa Pike is on Tennessee's death row for the 1995 killing of Colleen Slemmer.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth: Use the court's order or contemporaneous reporting to identify the court. Resolution Date: Resolve to the court that grants a stay of Pike's execution on September 30, 2026, before her scheduled execution time that day. Accepted Answer Format: Answer with its commonly used short name.
questions.current_reasoning: Key 2026-09-03 to 2026-09-14 legal and clemency developments (WVLT Sept 3; NewsNation Sept 4; Nashville Banner Sept 11 & 14; Death Penalty Information Center & Hindustan Times Sept 14): NewsNation reports the Tennessee Supreme Court rejected Pike's lethal-injection protocol challenge following Special Master Mark Ward's Aug 21 denial, and her Sept 30 execution date remains intact. Pike's legal team and supporters have pivoted heavily toward executive clemency—filing a 226-page clemency petition with Gov. Bill Lee (Sept 3), backed by 100+ anti-gender-violence organizations (Sept 11) and UN human rights experts + IACHR intervening today (Sept 14)—while a trauma-experts amicus brief was also filed with the Tennessee Supreme Court requesting a certificate of commutation. Because BOTH an executive clemency/reprieve by Gov. Lee (not a court), any pre-Sept-30 stay, AND execution proceeding on Sept 30 resolve to 'None', the failed protocol challenge and heavy clemency pivot raise 'None' from 0.63 to 0.68, trimming execution-day stay odds for U.S. Supreme Court (0.16 -> 0.14), Tennessee Supreme Court (0.10 -> 0.08), and Sixth Circuit (0.07 -> 0.06), with Davidson County Chancery Court unchanged at 0.02 (0.02 residual for M.D. Tenn. / TN Court of Appeals).
